strategy.summary: Reproduce NumPy PR #31433 (issue #31421): np.abs of a positive NaN yields a negative-signed NaN on wasm32/Pyodide because the buggy abs loops used tmp + 0 to clear -0.0, which corrupts NaN sign. Build NumPy at the buggy commit 723f2fbc453f from source, run the developer's test_abs_nan_signbit / test_abs_nan_signbit_array in numpy/_core/tests/test_umath.py; it should fail on buggy and pass on fixed. Native x86_64 Linux may not exhibit the defect, so the transition is only expected under wasm32/Emscripten or a faithful emulation.

pinned_because: numpy version is unconstrained by documentation; the reported 2.2.5 in issue #31421 is not a constraint for the fix, so the buggy checkout is built from source at 723f2fbc453f instead of pinning a wheel
pytest and hypothesis are documented in README.md but have no version constraint, so latest compatible versions are chosen

strategy.reproducing_test: test_abs_nan_signbit (parametrized over float16, float32, float64, longdouble) and test_abs_nan_signbit_array in numpy/_core/tests/test_umath.py
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 723f2fbc453f, test_abs_nan_signbit fails for at least one dtype (the abs(+nan) assertion) and/or test_abs_nan_signbit_array fails because np.signbit(np.abs(np.array([nan,-nan]))) contains True; on the fixed revision (fabs-based loops) all parametrizations and the array test pass.
strategy.numerical_probe: np.signbit(np.abs(np.float32(np.nan))) and np.signbit(np.abs(np.float64(np.nan))) and np.signbit(np.abs(np.longdouble(np.nan))) as the sign-bit check of +nan input

input_output_examples.buggy_output: negative NaN (np.signbit returns True) on wasm32/Pyodide

risks: The defect is platform-specific as reported (wasm32/Pyodide, Emscripten). On native x86_64 Linux or macOS the tmp + 0 idiom may not flip NaN sign, so the test may pass on buggy and the transition will not occur; this must be verified and the result reported honestly.
Reproducing on wasm32 requires an Emscripten/Pyodide toolchain build of NumPy, which is not assumed available; without it the transition cannot be demonstrated locally.
Passages disagree on which file holds the longdouble fix (PR body cites loops.c.src; diffs touch loops_unary_fp.dispatch.c.src); the buggy LONGDOUBLE_absolute path may need separate inspection.
Whether npy_fabs also preserves -0.0 clearing semantics is not stated in the evidence; the test only checks NaN sign so it does not grade that.
Compiler optimisation (e.g. -ffast-math or constant folding of tmp + 0) can change behaviour; use the default release-like debug build flags and record them.
float16 coverage is requested in discussion and listed as added in the diff; the test's float16 case depends on the float16 abs path being reached and may behave differently from float32/float64.
Test assertion text uses assert_ with a message; the message string is only printed on failure and is not a numerical check.

oracle.reference_source: numpy/_core/tests/test_umath.py test_abs_nan_signbit, which asserts np.signbit of the abs result is False
oracle.why: The defect is a sign-bit flip on NaN, a boolean property, so the oracle is exact equality of signbit to False rather than a numeric tolerance.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On the buggy revision on wasm32/Pyodide, np.signbit(np.abs(np.nan)) returns True, so the assertion 'not np.signbit(np.abs(pos_nan))' is False and the test raises AssertionError with the message 'abs(+nan) should have positive sign for <dtype>'. This only occurs on the affected platform; on native hardware the buggy code may not reproduce the failure.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision, abs uses npy_fabs/npy_fabsf/npy_fabsl, which clears the sign bit of NaN regardless of input sign, so signbit is False for both +nan and -nan across all four dtypes and for the array case, and the tests pass.
